blueprint_concepts: Common chord of two circles and its length

concept_use.Radical Axis and radical center: The point K where two common chords (radical axes) meet is the radical centre, so its power -20 is common to all three circles.
concept_use.Common chord of two circles and its leng: The common chord of C1 and C2 is x = 1 with ends A, B = (1, +-2 sqrt6), chord length 4 sqrt6; KA . KB is read on this chord.

english: Let $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}=25$, $C_{2}:x^{2}+y^{2}-6x-19=0$ and $C_{3}:x^{2}+y^{2}-4y-17=0$. The common chord of $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ meets $C_{1}$ at $A$ and $B$, and it intersects the common chord of $C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ at the point $K$. Then the value of $KA\cdot KB$ is ______.
solution: $K$: $x=1$, $4y=8\Rightarrow K=(1,2)$ (the radical centre, so its power is the same for all three circles)
Power of $K$ w.r.t. $C_{1}$: $1+4-25=-20<0$, so $K$ is inside $C_{1}$ and lies on chord $AB$
solution_full: Common chord of $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ (their radical axis): $S_{1}-S_{2}=6x-6=0$, i.e. $x=1$. It cuts $C_{1}$ where $y^{2}=24$, so the circles do intersect, at $A=(1,2\sqrt{6})$ and $B=(1,-2\sqrt{6})$; $AB=4\sqrt{6}$.
$K$: $x=1$ and $3-2y+1=0$, so $K=(1,2)$. $K$ lies on all three radical axes, so it is the radical centre: $S_{1}(K)=S_{2}(K)=S_{3}(K)$.
$S_{1}(K)=1+4-25=-20$ (also $S_{2}(K)=1+4-6-19=-20$), so $K$ is inside $C_{1}$ and lies between $A$ and $B$.
For a chord $AB$ of $C_{1}$ through the interior point $K$, $KA\cdot KB=r^{2}-OK^{2}=-S_{1}(K)=20$.
originality_note: New: the point K is defined as the meeting point of two common chords (the radical centre, never named), and the product KA . KB along the first common chord equals minus the common power (way 5, power of a point linked to the radical centre). Closest known: radical centre of three given circles; common chord length. Different because: the radical centre is used through the power of a point on a chord, not to build an orthogonal circle, and the answer is a product of segments.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, curve and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, and the Hindi mirrors the English. Rewrote the first draft, which defined K through equal tangent lengths and named the idea; K is now the meeting point of two common chords. Checked all three pairs intersect. Answer 20 is a positive 2-digit integer as planned.
key_step: K is the radical centre, so KA . KB = -S1(K) = 20 by the power of a point.
justification: Two radical axes, power of a point on a chord: a routine chain of standard results. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q2 (L2); much lighter than 2023-P2-Q13 (L4).
